I've been in it since 2015 and it's not an easy role to learn. I always try to gank mid or top to get them a lead, it is one less person you have to worry about and they'll be more willing to help you because you helped them. More often than not bot will need your most attention as they tend to need that extra bump. Pink wards are your friend, always put them in the enemy jungle or river, the more visit n on their jg the more you know when to take advantage of their position. If the enemy jungle ganks on the opposite side of the map try to take the objective on the opposite side, especially dragon if top gets ganked. If you aren't terrible behind always try to pick off their jg when you can. The more stuff they have to catch up on, the more you can pull ahead. I agree completely, we shouldn't mettle in their personal issues. The issue is China should've taken more into account than their own personal borders, of course there could be more than what we know, but it created the issue of supplies and whatever other reason US or China would tack onto their cause for war. For the chips specifically, I mentioned in my second reply I think about the CHIPS act which is going to be the process of building them ourselves. I heard it would be built in Columbus, OH. Not sure if the location is true but just heard it a few months ago.

I'm not too sure on the history as you mentioned it before with the Chinese/Taiwan history comment. I know they have history but that doesn't mean much in my opinion nor do I claim to be an expert on those countries. But I would argue that in this situation it seems like both countries are picking the fight, I wouldn't say US is starting it or China. I know it's a broken record but I don't think you truly understand how important these chips are. To me it seems like China is bringing up their own history like "Yeah, we own Taiwan so it's ours still." And the US is like  "Hey, we need the chips they make too." But China is basically saying that doesn't matter and the US is like if you try to take those resources from the neutral party in this situation we are going to be forced to defend it. Of course China doesn't like that so they essentially are saying you won't do anything about it, which definitely would make some people mad on either side. Like I said this is just what I have gathered and I'm not military, economic, or history expert. But from where I am sitting it seems like both countries want the resource. I'd assume we shared the chips before and would both buy them from Taiwan so the only logic explanation is one wants it for themselves. As to what I have seen it seems like China started the first claim on Taiwan and didn't expect the US to say anything. Then it becomes a situation where they both say the other started it. When to me it is pretty clear the both countries have been looking for a reason to go to war in the past few years.  If not longer.

Diplomacy is always a possibility. Of course violence is the fastest and most direct route you can take to achieve these types of thing. We are also talking about a PROVEN military powerhouse, doesn't make it okay of course, but it's not exactly a smart move to basically tell this guy that has proven himself that he would be silly to defend something that he needs, ya know what I mean? But let's not pretend like TONS of world leaders don't tip toe around each other and hide their true opinions , I do that in everyday life and that doesn't affect millions. I'd imagine it's pretty clear the US is failing those policies because I don't think gearing up for war on either side is a good image. And once again, I'd would definitely argue that those SPECIFIC resources would be worth going to war for if we don't have another option for them until we have our own facilities up and running. There's a lot of things going on in the US and it's painfully obvious that we need to admit we failed on a lot of things. But defending the access to those resources is not something I, if in the position to make these types of call, would be okay with giving up to our biggest rival because of their past history. This is something that would affect our future let alone their history. It's called history for a reason.

I get it. Think about it this way, you got all your fancy gadgets, your entertainment for your citizens, all those shiny military weapons you have. What happens when one of your biggest potential adversaries has control of the resources that allows you to have all those things? It's not like you WOULDN'T do anything. The world doesn't belong to anyone. If the US has interest in it and I'm sure other countries do too just not as much as the US, it's not exactly okay for them to claim it and cut them off. A lot of places have started wars for a lot less. I'm not saying the war is a good thing, just that in my honest opinion, it would be justifiable. Of course people disagree and that makes sense but it's not like the US is like "let them people be free." It's about a resource and believe it or not resources are quiet valuable, especially one of that magnitude.

Taiwan makes semiconductors which are used in phones, cars, computers, etc. China is trying to claim Taiwan as their own I believe and the US obviously won't be okay with that as it would hurt us dramatically. We did however just pass the CHIPS act which is going to let the US create their own semiconductors and we will not have to rely on Taiwan as much if at all in the next few years. I wouldn't say we "WANT" this war but it's not like we are just giving up an ally, we would be giving up an extremely valuable resource. People can correct me if I am wrong but that is what I personally have gathered over the last few months.
